question.title: Will Swiss voters approve the "No to a Switzerland with 10 million" population cap referendum?
question.description:
According to the [Federal Council](https://www.admin.ch/en/sustainability-initiative) (the official website of the Swiss government): 

> At the end of 2025, approximately 9.1 million people were living in Switzerland. Since the introduction of the free movement of persons in 2002, the population has grown by around 1.7 million. This is mainly due to immigration. The number of people immigrating depends primarily on the labour market. When the economy is strong, companies struggle to find enough workers within Switzerland. Companies, as well as public institutions like hospitals and care homes, often recruit the skilled workers they need from the EU.

> The ‘No to a Switzerland with 10 million! (Sustainability Initiative)’ calls for a cap on the permanent resident population: Switzerland’s population must remain below 10 million until 2050. If the permanent resident population exceeds 9.5 million before 2050, the Federal Council and Parliament will need to take measures, particularly in the areas of asylum and family reunification. The Federal Council would also need to invoke or negotiate exemptions and safeguard clauses in international agreements that contribute to population growth. If the 10-million threshold is exceeded, Switzerland would have to terminate these agreements, including the one with the EU on the free movement of persons after two years. This would also render the other agreements under Bilateral Agreements I null and void. Switzerland’s participation in the EU’s Schengen and Dublin agreements would also be called into question, thereby jeopardising close cooperation in the areas of security and asylum.

In order to pass, an initiative [requires](https://www.ch.ch/en/votes-and-elections/votes/popular-majority-and-majority-of-the-cantons/#when-is-a-popular-majority-and-a-majority-of-the-cantons-required) a "double majority" of both the popular majority nationally and the popular vote within a majority of Switzerland's cantons to vote yes. 

Polling has been as follows:

| Pollster / sponsor                                                                                                                                             |            Fieldwork | Yes |  No | Undecided |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------: | --: | --: | --------: |
| [YouGov Switzerland](https://yougov.com/de-de/artikel/54847-zwischenstand-stimmungsbarometer-eidgenoessischen-abstimmungen-vom-14-juni-2026)                   |      May 18–26, 2026 | 43% | 51% |        6% |
| [SRG / gfs.bern](https://www.srf.ch/news/schweiz/1-srg-umfrage-pattsituation-bei-keine-10-mio-schweiz-initiative)                                              |  Apr. 20–May 3, 2026 | 47% | 47% |        6% |
| [YouGov Switzerland](https://yougov.com/de-de/artikel/54695-was-denkt-die-schweiz-uber-die-nachhaltigkeitsinitiative-und-die-anderung-des-zivildienstgesetzes) |  Apr. 21–May 4, 2026 | 45% | 46% |        8% |
| [20 Minuten / Tamedia / LeeWas](https://www.tamedia.ch/news/knappe-mehrheit-fuer-nachhaltigkeitsinitiative-offenes-rennen-um-zivildienstgesetz)                |     Apr. 22–23, 2026 | 52% | 46% |        2% |
| [Tamedia / LeeWas](https://www.blick.ch/politik/abstimmungskrimi-bahnt-sich-an-gegner-der-10-millionen-initiative-haben-knapp-die-nase-vorn-id21789514.html)   |           March 2026 | 45% | 47% |        8% |
| [Sotomo / ](https://sotomo.ch/site/projekte/kampagnenbefragung-10-millionen-schweiz/)                                                                          | Jun. 25–Jul. 4, 2025 | 48% | 45% |        7% |
| [LeeWas / Tamedia](https://www.tamedia.ch/news/knappe-mehrheit-fuer-nachhaltigkeitsinitiative-offenes-rennen-um-zivildienstgesetz)                             |            Nov. 2025 | 48% | 41% |       11% |

question.title: Will Donald Trump's name be removed from the Kennedy Center's exterior signage before July 1, 2026?
question.description:
AP July 12, 2026: [Judge denies Kennedy Center request for pause in ruling ordering Trump’s name removed from building](https://apnews.com/article/trump-name-kennedy-center-e6caa6a7c6115671490278491ee9e96c)

> A judge on Friday denied a request from the Kennedy Center to pause a ruling ordering President Donald Trump’s name removed from building.

> Unless the Kennedy Center decides to appeal the decision from U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper, the decision raises the prospect that Trump’s name will be removed from the building. In his ruling last month, Cooper said only Congress could institute a change to the Kennedy Center’s name and ordered that references to Trump be removed by Friday.

> A Kennedy Center spokesperson didn’t immediately comment on the ruling. Workers were seen building scaffolding around a section of the building that includes Trump’s name.

> Last month, Cooper ruled Trump’s name was illegally added to the iconic Washington performing arts facility. Late Thursday, Trump’s handpicked board at the center mounted a last-minute effort to keep his name on the facade of the iconic performing arts facility but Cooper refused to stay his order.

Trump's name [was added ](https://www.nbcwashington.com/news/local/trumps-name-being-removed-from-kennedy-center-exterior/4115993/)to the signage in December 2025:

![](https://cdn.metaculus.com/user_uploaded/Screenshot-2026-06-12-132318.webp)
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as Yes if before July 1, 2026, according to [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) Donald Trump’s name is removed from the building facade signage at the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts.

question.title: How many Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy launches will SpaceX conduct between May 28, 2026 and June 14, 2026?
question.description:
SpaceX operates the Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy launch vehicles, with Falcon 9 being its workhorse rocket flying multiple Starlink, government, and commercial missions per week. In 2025 SpaceX conducted a record number of Falcon launches, and the 2026 cadence has continued at a similar pace. As of May 30, 2026, the Falcon 9 family had logged 656 launches total, with roughly 60 Falcon 9 launches in 2026 year-to-date. Starship remains separate (and is not counted in this question). Recent May 2026 activity shows roughly 9-10 Falcon 9 launches in the month, with confirmed launches on May 29 (Starlink Group 10-53) and May 30 (Starlink Group 17-41). The 18-day window covered by this question (May 28 through June 13, 2026 inclusive) historically corresponds to about 5-7 Falcon launches at current cadence.

`{"format": "llm_question", "info": {"rating": {"quality": 3, "ambiguity": 4, "resolvability": 4, "passes": true}}}`
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the number of orbital launches of the Falcon 9 or Falcon Heavy rocket conducted by SpaceX with liftoff occurring on or after 00:00 UTC on May 28, 2026 and before 00:00 UTC on June 14, 2026, as listed in the Wikipedia article 'List of Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy launches' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Falcon_9_and_Falcon_Heavy_launches). A launch counts if the vehicle lifts off from the pad during the window, regardless of whether the mission ultimately succeeds or fails (i.e., partial failures and in-flight failures still count as launches). A pad abort or scrubbed attempt where the vehicle does not lift off does NOT count. For example, if 7 Falcon 9 launches occur in this window, the answer is '7'. If the Wikipedia page is unavailable or has not been updated, the resolver may use SpaceX's official launches page (https://www.spacex.com/launches) or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) to count the launches.
question.fine_print: Only Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy launches are counted; Starship launches are excluded. Static fire tests and wet dress rehearsals do not count. Liftoff time is determined in UTC.

question.title: What will the WastewaterSCAN national wastewater category for Norovirus GII be for the week ending June 13, 2026?
question.description:
[WastewaterSCAN](https://data.wastewaterscan.org/) is a wastewater surveillance program run by Stanford, Emory, and Verily that tracks pathogens in sewage across hundreds of U.S. treatment plants. For Norovirus GII (a major cause of acute gastroenteritis), the dashboard reports a national "Wastewater Category" of Low, Medium, or High based on a combination of: (1) the 21-day concentration trend, (2) the current level relative to tertile bands of all measurements over the past 365 days, and (3) frequency of detection. If no sample has been collected in the last 7 days, the category is reported as "Not Calculated."

Norovirus is highly seasonal in the U.S., typically peaking in late winter and declining through spring into summer. During the 2025–2026 season, monthly WastewaterSCAN updates classified national Norovirus GII as HIGH in February and March 2026, driven in part by the GII.17 variant. As of the dashboard reading on May 30, 2026, national Norovirus GII has dropped to the Medium category with no clear 21-day trend. Historically, by mid-June, norovirus levels often decline further into Low, but the lingering tail of the GII.17 wave introduces uncertainty about whether levels will fall, stay Medium, or rebound.

`{"format": "llm_question", "info": {"rating": {"quality": 3, "ambiguity": 3, "resolvability": 4, "passes": true}}}`
question.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves based on the national "Wastewater Category" shown for Norovirus GII (target "Noro_G2") on the [WastewaterSCAN national dashboard](https://data.wastewaterscan.org/) when viewed for the National location, reflecting data through the week ending Saturday, June 13, 2026. The question will be resolved using the dashboard reading taken between June 14 and June 17, 2026 (whichever first reflects samples through the week ending June 13, 2026).

- "Low" resolves if the dashboard's national status label for Norovirus is "low".
- "Medium" resolves if the label is "medium".
- "High" resolves if the label is "high".
- "Not Calculated / Other" resolves if the dashboard shows "Not Calculated," "Not Detected," or no category is displayed for the national Norovirus GII view.

If the WastewaterSCAN dashboard is unavailable, the corresponding WastewaterSCAN monthly nationwide update post on https://wwscan.ghost.io/ covering June 2026 will be used as a fallback. If neither source provides a national Norovirus GII category by June 17, 2026, the question resolves as "Not Calculated / Other."
question.fine_print: If WastewaterSCAN renames the category labels (e.g., "Moderate" instead of "Medium"), the equivalent middle-tier label resolves as "Medium." Only the national-level reading is used; regional readings are ignored.
